ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL runtime crash after login/register: `setMessages(claimThread(...))` set state to the response object {messages:[...]} instead of the array. DevotionalStream then threw 'messages.map is not a function' and the Emergent runtime-error overlay appeared, breaking the auth flow. Fixed by unwrapping res.messages. Same pattern was safer for loadAuthThread (already unwrapped in lib/auth.js).

action_items: Review the App.js handleAuthed fix (unwrapping claimThread response). Trivially applied by testing agent.
Consider adding an ErrorBoundary around DevotionalStream so future prop-shape bugs don't crash the whole UI with the runtime overlay.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js:244 handleAuthed passed the raw response object of claimThread({token}) directly to setMessages — but claimThread returns {messages:[...]} (see lib/auth.js post()). This is a shape-mismatch bug; loadAuthThread() already unwraps .messages but claimThread() does not. Recommend normalizing lib/auth.js:claimThread to return the array (parity with loadAuthThread) so callers cannot repeat this mistake.

server.py:/api/auth/claim silently migrates ANY provided anon token — no ownership proof — so a signed-in user who guesses/knows another device's session token could claim its thread. Session tokens are 128-bit random from lib/api.js, so exploitability is low, but consider requiring the anon token to have been established client-side within the same auth session (e.g. via signed cookie) before claim, or at least logging + rate-limiting claims.

server.py set_auth_cookie uses samesite='none'; secure=True; httpOnly=True — good. However cookie is issued even in local http contexts which would silently drop; not a preview-env problem but worth documenting.

server.py seed_admin still uses ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD envs to seed 'seeker@mahakalistudios.com'. If credentials change, seed_admin rehashes on next boot — good idempotency. Bcrypt hash format verified via login test ($2b$).
Frontend: no ErrorBoundary anywhere; a single render-time bug (like the one fixed) takes down the entire chat surface.

server.py /api/tts/generate rate-limits per-user or per-client-host — behind a proxy request.client.host may be the ingress IP, effectively coalescing all anon users into one bucket. Consider using X-Forwarded-For.

rca of the issue: Bug: post-register/login runtime crash 'messages.map is not a function'. Reproduction: activate app → menu → Save & sync thread → register or login → within 1s the Emergent runtime overlay appears and the app is unusable. Root cause: App.js handleAuthed did `const msgs = await claimThread(token); setMessages(msgs)`; claimThread returns the raw JSON `{messages:[...]}` (via lib/auth.js post()) instead of the array. loadAuthThread already unwraps .messages, so the two helpers had inconsistent shapes and the caller assumed 'array'. Fix (applied): setMessages(Array.isArray(res) ? res : res?.messages || []) with the same defensive check in the catch branch. Mitigation for future: normalize claimThread to return data.messages in lib/auth.js, and wrap DevotionalStream in an ErrorBoundary.
